target_customer: Blind and visually impaired people, sold directly and through distributors such as Vision Australia
problem: White canes and guide dogs miss obstacles above waist height, and blind users want better spatial awareness.
business_model: Hardware sales of the Sunu Band at 299 USD in 2017, with crowdfunding and distributors

founders.name: Marco Trujillo
founders.background_notes: The YC page says he built hardware products used by thousands of blind and visually impaired people.

founders.name: Fernando Albertorio
founders.background_notes: The YC page describes 13 years of product work in AI, wearables and digital health. Press describes him as legally blind and a daily user.

founders.name: Cuauhtli Padilla
founders.background_notes: No further background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware combining a sonar sensor, haptic feedback, battery life and wearable industrial design, produced in small volume by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and distributor relationships gave some barrier, but no patents or data advantages were found in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ars Technica coverage in 2017 noted that other companies already made similar wearable obstacle detectors, but no incumbent copying or buying Sunu was found.

market_need_then: Press in August 2017 described unmet mobility needs for blind users and shipping at 299 USD, with sales through a Vision Australia distribution deal. Crowdfunding claims by the company exceeded its goal, which is unverified.

branding.domain_note: sunu.com now redirects to a domain-name marketplace listing, so the company's original .com is no longer used.

identity.voice_and_tone: Superpowers framing: equipping blind users with super powers per YC

branding.brand_signature: Sunu Band sonar wristband with vibration that grows as objects get closer

rebrands.why: A single profile says Sunu was formerly Ustraap; no reason or date was found.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in MIT Technology Review, Wareable and Digital Trends in 2017; the company reports a crowdfunding campaign above its goal, which is unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Good press for a small hardware company, but limited evidence of community or brand pull beyond early coverage.

pivots.to: Sunu Nek, a neck-worn AR interface with radar, audio and haptics
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page describes the neck-worn product and an aim to serve everyone.

outcome_analysis: Sunu built a sonar wristband for blind users and later a neck-worn radar interface, with a founder who is himself a user. YC lists it as inactive, yet other profiles show a 2019 seed and a 2021 style crowdfunding raise, and no closure was found. Without a source for shutdown or the cause, the outcome is unknown and no failure factors are recorded.
notes: Totals conflict: Seedtable 620K total, CB Insights 830K over 5 rounds, Techleap 564K euros; the 400K seed in 2019-03 rests on a single database (Seedtable). CB Insights names Republic, Bossa Invest, Ark Fund, Indiegogo and Y Combinator among investors without round detail, and Crowdability adds Toushka Capital and Avalancha Ventures; these are not tied to rounds. Company site sunu.com redirects to a domain broker listing, so the site is dead. YC says inactive but no shutdown evidence was found. Dated 2017 competitor search found only an unnamed mention of similar wearables in Ars Technica via a reprint; CB Insights peer pages are undated, so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers were not found. Dating of the Ustraap former name rests on one profile.
